candidates.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
support_spans: She was receiving milrinone at home through a double lumen tunneled catheter.
Tunneled catheter site showed no erythema, warmth, drainage, or tenderness
Initial blood culture from tunneled catheter: positive at 7.2 hours
Gram stain from all three sets showed gram-negative bacilli
candidates.why: The patient has a tunneled catheter and developed symptoms of infection, with positive blood cultures from the catheter and peripheral sites, indicating a catheter-related bloodstream infection.

candidates.name: Sepsis
support_spans: Four days before presentation, she developed cough and chills.
Later developed: Temperature of 39°C
Leukocyte count: 12.4 ×10³/µL (normal 4.0-11.0 ×10³/µL)
C-reactive protein: 158 mg/L (normal, <8 mg/L)
candidates.why: The patient presents with signs of infection, including fever, chills, and elevated inflammatory markers, indicating sepsis.

candidates.name: Gram-negative bacteremia
support_spans: Gram stain from all three sets showed gram-negative bacilli
Initial blood culture from tunneled catheter: positive at 7.2 hours
Additional peripheral blood culture: positive at 5.13 hours
Additional catheter blood culture: positive at 8.3 hours
candidates.why: The patient has positive blood cultures with gram-negative bacilli, indicating gram-negative bacteremia.
